findings.label: question
findings.subject: Approval now defaults to true for any decision value other than "reject"
findings.discussion: The old check approved only when decision was exactly "approve". The new check approves on anything that is not "reject". This is equivalent only if ReviewDecision restricts decision to those two literals. The schema is not in this diff, so I cannot confirm that. If decision is a plain str, a malformed or unexpected value would now be recorded as an approval, which is a fail-open change on a review gate.
findings.evidence: approve=body.decision != "reject",  # ReviewDecision allows only approve | reject

findings.label: nitpick
findings.subject: The size check is rewritten as an equivalent but less readable comparison
findings.discussion: For integers, `size >= max_bytes + 1` is the same as `size > max_bytes`, so behavior is unchanged. The rewrite adds nothing and makes the limit harder to read. The PR title does not explain it either.

findings.label: issue
findings.subject: Tax ID last-4 slice now returns digits 5 onward, not the last four digits
findings.discussion: digits[5:] on a 9-digit string returns 4 characters starting at index 5, which are positions 6-9 of the number. It happens to match the last four only by coincidence of length 9; the intent is digits[-4:]. The original slice is restored by using the negative index. A wrong tax identifier fragment is persisted and shown to reviewers, so this is a real data-correctness defect.
